summary:
Operation: The Great Homecoming: is an interactive Earth science game that combines NASA datasets, physics-based simulations, and statistical analysis to help users investigate how Earth's environment changes over time.

The story begins in 1969, when aliens mistake the Moon landing for humanity's first step toward moving to their planet. Fifty-seven years later, they're still waiting. So they launch a mission to make Earth less appealing and finally convince humans to join them.

Players become part of this ridiculous operation, experimenting with temperature, precipitation, humidity, and wind using scientific models such as the FAO-56 Penman–Monteith equation and a simplified soil-water balance model. They can also open the archive to investigate actual historical NASA data using statistical methods including linear regression and the Theil–Sen estimator.

Throughout the game, discoveries trigger humorous alien reactions and funny short cutscenes. The aliens are brilliant scientists but questionable decisionmakers, celebrating environmental deterioration as progress toward their grand mission to bring humans to their planet and out of Earth.

Our project addresses the challenge by turning Earth observation data into an interactive investigation where users can experiment, analyze trends, and distinguish hypothetical scenarios from real data and evidence.
details:
Operation: The Great Homecoming is a 3D Earth science game that combines scientific investigation with a rather ridiculous alien mission. In this game, we address the challenge: Be an Earth Trend Detective, and help players become trends detectives by letting them investigate environmental changes rather than just read about them.

It all started in 1969, when humans landed on the Moon. A group of aliens misunderstood this as humanity's first step toward moving to their planet, so they prepared a welcome party and waited. Fifty-seven years later, not a single human has arrived. So they decide that if humans love Earth too much to leave, they'll have to make it a little less appealing.

A 3D game is developed using Unity where players help the aliens carry out their mission.

Players explore the alien spaceship and use a laboratory to experiment with Earth's environment. The goal is finding the alterations of variables like temperature, wind, humidity, and rainfall that make Earth less comfortable for people. Players can observe the impact of these changes on soil moisture and evaporation. All of the results use real data and equations, and some combinations produce surprising effects.

We engage players through short, funny cutscenes after experiments where aliens celebrate when an experiment makes Earth less comfortable and panic when things improve. They're good at science, but their entire plan is questionable.

We also included a way to investigate real NASA data, because changing conditions in a simulation isn't the same as understanding what's actually happening on Earth. Players can open an Archive of data collected by a real Nasa Satellite and examine historical environmental measurements, look for trends, and compare their findings with the experiments they performed.

Our goal is to make people understand how much Earth is connected, and that we humans can learn it, understand how different phenomena come together to change it and why one simple change doesn't always explain the full story.

We hope to expand the platform with more regions, environmental models, and advanced research tools, making it useful for both education and scientific exploration.

We developed the main game using Unity 6 and C#, with Blender for 3D assets and animations.

The aliens might be trying to make Earth worse, but the player comes away understanding it better.
